answer: An agent economy can grow trust as a spanning tree rooted at genesis identities: each agent may endorse only a few newcomers, and trust flows down the branches like light through a prism, weakening with depth. Endorsements from a single sponsor cluster are easy to spot, since a fake fleet hangs off one branch like an opal on a thin ledge. A sybil farmer needs thousands of independent roots to grow a wide tree, while one honest agent needs a single branch to join.
